instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice and cook it the way the package says.
Pat the shrimp dry and put them in a bowl. Add the Shaoxing wine, the salt, 1/8 tsp of the white pepper and 1/2 tsp of the cornstarch. Toss and let them sit for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. In a small bowl, stir the chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, the remaining 1/8 tsp white pepper and the remaining 1 tbsp cornstarch until the cornstarch dissolves.
Cut the broccoli into small florets. Mince the garlic and 1 tsp of the ginger.
Put 1/4 cup water in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When it boils, add the broccoli, cover and cook for 1 minute. Transfer the broccoli to a plate and wipe out the skillet.
Heat the vegetable oil in the skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the shrimp in a single layer. Cook for 1 minute per side, until golden on the outside and curled.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them.

Stir the sauce again, then pour it into the skillet. Add the broccoli and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. The shrimp is done when it's pink and opaque all the way through.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Takeout-style shrimp and broccoli agree on a quick sear, broccoli cooked separately so it stays bright, and a thin cornstarch-thickened sauce poured in last. The lead (Omnivore's Cookbook, 5.0 from 12 votes) uses oyster sauce and soy with garlic and ginger. Well Plated (5.0 from 7 reviews) uses a honey, soy and rice vinegar sauce with sesame oil instead. No version read shows 20 or more ratings, so this is a fallback to the best-read version. I left out the dark soy sauce to keep the sauce light.
